newsitem.title: GERMANY: German institutes see 4.3 mln jobless in 97-source.
newsitem.headline: German institutes see 4.3 mln jobless in 97-source.

text.p: Germany's six leading economic research institutes expect unemployment to average 4.3 million this year and economic growth to be 2.5 percent, government sources said on Friday.
The sources had gained access to the institutes' half-yearly report -- whose figures are used as a basis for drafting the budget -- ahead of publication next Tuesday.
The institutes' forecast of growth in real gross domestic product confirmed the government's own prediction. But the unemployment figure exceeded Bonn's last forecast in January by 200,000.
The sources could not confirm earlier newspaper reports that the institutes would say next week that the budget deficit would be equivalent to 3.2 percent of GDP.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel has said that, despite higher unemployment, he would cut the budget deficit this year below the limit of three percent of GDP set by the Maastricht treaty to enable Germany to qualify for European monetary union.
The opposition Social Democrats (SPD) said earlier on Friday that federal borrowing was running out of control and urged the government to pass a supplementary budget.
